Asymmetric smoothed-association matrix

Source: R/janusplot.R
janusplot.Rd

Fits every ordered pair of numeric variables with janusplot_fit() and draws the matrix with plot.janusplot_fit() in one call. Each cell [r, c] off the diagonal shows the fitted spline of gam(x_r ~ s(x_c) + <adjust>) from mgcv::gam() or mgcv::bam(): the row variable on the vertical axis against the column variable on the horizontal axis, as in graphics::pairs(). The diagonal is blank; the variable names sit on the border and a key in the top-left corner shows the convention.

The two triangles differ by design: the asymmetry reveals heteroscedasticity, leverage and directional non-linearity that a single scalar correlation hides.

Usage

janusplot(
  data,
  vars = NULL,
  adjust = NULL,
  colour_by = "nonlinearity",
  background_by = NULL,
  annotations = NULL,
  order = "original",
  display = "fit",
  group = NULL,
  focus_by = NA_character_,
  focus_threshold = "q90",
  axes = "original",
  style = janusplot_style(),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame. Column names need not be syntactic; fits run under internal aliases and every result reports the original names.

vars

Character vector of numeric column names to fit, in matrix order. NULL (the default) takes every numeric column of data. Identical or exactly collinear columns are not fitted against each other; their cells are listed in flags$failed.

adjust

One-sided formula of covariates and random effects added to every pairwise model, for example ~ s(age) + s(site, bs = "re"). NULL (the default) fits unadjusted smooths. Character and logical adjust columns are converted to factor before fitting. Random-effect smooths are excluded from prediction, so the curve and its band are population-level. With the identity link (the Gaussian default) the curve is the smooth averaged over the adjustment covariates of the data, and the plots draw each point as a partial residual: the observation with its own adjustment replaced by that average, so points and curve share one level (style$adjusted_points). With another link, numeric covariates are held at their mean and fixed factors at their most frequent level, and points stay raw.

colour_by

The quantity painted on each cell: "nonlinearity" (the default; EDF minus 1 of the cell's smooth, sequential from 0), "asymmetry" (the pair's index A in [0, 1], the same in both cells), "pearson", "spearman" or "kendall" (the pair's correlation on a diverging scale over [-1, 1]), "deviance_gap" (deviance explained by the smooth minus the straight line's) or "none".

background_by

The correlation that tints each cell's background: "pearson", "spearman", "kendall", or "none" for no background. Left unset, it is "pearson" for a marginal fit and "none" for a fit with adjust, whose curves are adjusted while the correlations are marginal; set it to show the marginal correlation behind adjusted curves. Independent of colour_by. It cannot be combined with janusplot_style(colour_channel = "fill"), which paints the same area.

annotations

Character vector, a subset of c("A", "edf", "signif", "code", "shape", "k_warn", "n", "r", "formula"), written in the strip of every cell (or in its corners under janusplot_style(annotation_position = "corners")): the asymmetry index, the EDF, the significance glyph of the smooth F-test (*** p < .001, ** p < .01, * p < .05, . p < .1, from the adjusted p-value when the fit has p_adjust other than "none"), the two-letter shape code, the shape glyph, a warning sign on cells flagged by the k-check or capped at the distinct predictor count, the rows used, the background_by correlation of the pair (Pearson when background_by = "none"), printed "r -0.03" ("marginal r -0.03" for a fit with adjust), and the cell's formula, printed Temp ~ Ozone. NULL (the default) picks by matrix size: c("A", "signif") up to twelve variables, "signif" from thirteen, where 5-point strips of neighbouring cells would touch; character() writes none.

order

Order of the variables in the matrix: "original" (the default, the order of x$vars), "hclust" (hierarchical clustering of absolute Pearson correlations) or "alphabetical". Drawing only; the fit is unchanged.

display

What every off-diagonal cell shows: "fit" (the default), "d1" (the first derivative of the smooth, whose zero crossings are turning points) or "d2" (the second derivative, whose zero crossings are inflections). A derivative view needs the fit to carry that order in x$settings$derivatives.

group

Name of a factor, character or logical column of x$data whose levels colour the raw points, with one legend below the matrix, or NULL (the default). Drawing only; the column never enters the model. The column must exist in x$data and have at most style$group_max_levels levels.

focus_by

NA (the default, no filter) or one of "asymmetry", "edf", "non_linearity" (EDF minus 1) and "k_flag". Cells whose metric falls below focus_threshold are washed in grey at style$focus_dim_alpha; the matrix keeps its shape. A visual filter only; the fit and its table are unchanged.

focus_threshold

A quantile string, "q90" by default (taken over the off-diagonal cells), or a single numeric cutoff. Ignored when focus_by is NA.

axes

Scale of the drawn axes: "original" (the default), "standardised" ((x - mean) / sd per variable, border label "var (z)"), "centred" (x - mean, label "var (centred)") or "rank" (empirical rank, label "rank(var)"). Drawing only; the same transform is applied to the points, the curve and the band.

style

A janusplot_style() object holding every appearance setting.

...

Model arguments of janusplot_fit(), further arguments to mgcv::gam() or mgcv::bam(), and for one release the 0.2.0 appearance arguments listed in Details.

Value

A patchwork object, which is a ggplot, as described in plot.janusplot_fit(). With the deprecated with_data = TRUE, a list with elements plot (that object) and data (the per-cell table of summary.janusplot_fit()).

Details

Model settings (k, bs, engine, method, na_action, n_grid, derivatives, derivative_ci, derivative_ci_nsim, p_adjust, shape_cutoffs, k_check_thresholds, auto_refit_k, k_max_iter, discrete, nthreads, parallel, keep_fits) pass through ... to janusplot_fit(), which forwards anything else to mgcv. Appearance settings live in janusplot_style() and are passed as style. To draw the same fit more than once, call janusplot_fit() and plot() it.

The 0.2.0 appearance arguments of janusplot() are accepted through ... for one release, each with a deprecation warning, and are removed in 1.1.0: show_data, show_ci, palette, show_shape_legend, glyph_style, labels, diagonal, label_srt, show_glossary, compact, compact_threshold, compact_levels and focus_dim_alpha are applied to style; label_cex, text_scale_diag, text_scale_off_diag and glossary_scale are mapped to the labels, diagonal, strip and glossary elements of janusplot_style(text_size = ) at the matrix's variable count, close to but not exactly the 0.2.0 sizes; fill_by is mapped to colour_by; show_asymmetry and signif_glyph are mapped to annotations; labels = "diagonal" is drawn as "border" with a message; with_data = TRUE returns list(plot, data) with data the table of summary(janusplot_fit(...)); save_as, save_width, save_height and save_dpi write the plot once with ggplot2::ggsave(). Arguments after adjust must be named: the positional order of 0.2.0 is not shimmed.

See also

janusplot_fit() for the object behind the plot, plot.janusplot_fit() for the view arguments, janusplot_style() for the appearance settings.

Other smooth-associations: janusplot_compare(), janusplot_curves(), janusplot_direction(), janusplot_fit(), janusplot_pair(), janusplot_reference(), janusplot_style(), plot.janusplot_compare(), plot.janusplot_fit()

Examples

# Three variables, six asymmetric pairwise GAM fits.
janusplot(mtcars[, c("mpg", "hp", "wt")], engine = "gam")


# Other colourings, groups and the derivative displays
# (display = "d1", "d2") are shown in vignette("janusplot").
